inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted 193,954,539 from the H1-2026 interim report EPS note 3 (basic 190,597,758). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so compounding the count as well would double-charge the same cost. UCB buys treasury shares (EUR 127m H1-2026, EUR 121m FY2025) which broadly funds the flat count.
inputs.net_debt_basis: H1-2026 company-stated net financial debt EUR 2,821m (0.8x adj EBITDA): bonds 1,425 + bank borrowings 1,804 + debentures 150 + lease liabilities 209 = 3,588 total debt, less cash 766. USES THE H1-2026 BALANCE SHEET, not the FY2025 near-net-cash position (EUR -7m), because the Candid (USD 2.2bn) and Neurona (USD 1.15bn) acquisitions closed June 2026 and are the current state.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report consolidated cash flow note 37/28, 'Share-based payments to employees and directors' EUR 188m (FY2024: 183m). UCB discloses no separate equity-award withholding-tax line, so no add-on; the CSV StockBasedComp column is annual-only and NULL for all H1 periods, per instruction annual SBC is used and no H1 figure was derived.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, 10-year component build, scenario-weighted. Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md -- UCB is a conventional branded-biopharma operating company whose value is a forward free-cash-flow stream, so row 1/2 of the routing table (owner-FCF DCF) applies. No prior DCF exists and MEMORY.md has no UCB.BR entry, so this is a fresh build. Section 7 adaptations applied because UCB is a non-US (EUR) filer. || BASE FCF: last_fcf = 1842 reported - 188 SBC - 46 interest income = 1608 owner FCF. Interest income IS stripped (net cash was material at FY2025); the matching asset is in the bridge. || LEASES: treatment (A), leases as debt -- lease principal (EUR 60m FY2025, 31m H1-2026) is NOT deducted from the flows, and lease liabilities of EUR 209m ARE inside the EUR 3,588m total debt in the net-debt bridge. Charged once. lease_cost_pct is therefore 0.0. || NCI: nil. UCB reports non-controlling interests of EUR 0m in every year FY2022-FY2025, so no attributable-flow adjustment and no NCI stock deduction is needed. || WACC: 8.0%, built in EUR, the flows' own currency. 10y Bund ~2.8% (ECB hiked 25bp June 2026) + EUR ERP 5.0% x beta ~1.0 = 7.8% cost of equity; after-tax cost of debt ~3.2% at 6% weight gives a CAPM WACC of ~7.7%. Rounded UP to 8.0% -- the single deliberate premium -- for the single-asset Bimzelx concentration and for the US MFN/tariff exposure that management explicitly EXCLUDES from guidance, i.e. a risk that is by construction absent from the guided flows. This sits at the lower half of the 7.5-9.5% band and reflects that UCB is a EUR 42bn large cap with no illiquidity premium. RISK IS CHARGED ONCE: the same 8.0% WACC is used in all three scenarios; all other risk (LOE erosion, biosimilars, pricing) lives in the scenario flows, not in the discount rate. || WORKING CAPITAL: wc_capture is NEGATIVE (-12% base). UCB is not a prepaid-subscription business -- growth consumes cash into receivables and inventory. H1-2026 showed a EUR -623m working-capital outflow on 22% revenue growth, and FY2025's +303m inflow was the exception. Modelling this as a positive capture would have been a material overstatement.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: YES -- large divergence, and it is the central analytical fact about this name. Equity 5yr CAGR 8.4% vs FCF 5yr 20.6% and EPS 3yr 55.0% -- a >30% divergence on every pairing. The equity CAGR is NOT usable as the growth driver here: UCB pays out ~EUR 264m/yr in dividends and its book value is dominated by goodwill and intangibles from a prior acquisition era, so book growth describes capital structure rather than the Bimzelx-driven earnings inflection. Revenue CAGR is used as the anchor instead and is itself cross-checked against FY2026 guidance.
historical_growth.notes: All FCF CAGRs are computed on the OWNER-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less interest income) applied across the whole history, not on reported FCF. Owner FCF: FY2020 631, FY2021 934, FY2022 647, FY2023 321, FY2024 708, FY2025 1608. The owner and reported CAGRs are near-identical (35.5 vs 35.0 3yr) because UCB's SBC is only ~2.4% of revenue -- a normal European pharma level, nothing like a US software issuer. FY2015 owner FCF is negative (-45), so a 10-year CAGR is not computable and is not reported. IMPORTANT: the FY2015-2024 owner-FCF median of EUR 605m is NOT the base for this model -- see valuation_philosophy.

base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

bull.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

bear.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

entry_price.notes: Entry price is the price at which buying today, collecting the 10 years of projected owner FCF and exiting at the scenario's own terminal value earns a 15% IRR. Terminal value is computed at WACC (it is the fair price a buyer pays at exit); only the discounting back to today uses 15%. The weighted EUR 116.98 is ~46% below the market price -- a 15% IRR is simply not available in this name at EUR 216.50 on any scenario, including the bull case (bull entry EUR 184.08).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's required return (min(Gordon@r, cap x FCF_N)), so the flows and the exit are charged the same rate. Corrected 2026-09-01.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC 6-10%, columns terminal growth 1.0-3.0%. Flat cells at low WACC and high terminal growth are the 18x terminal cap binding -- Gordon there implies an exit multiple no buyer has to grant. House pair is WACC 8.0% / g 2.0% = EUR 206.80.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25 bear / 50 base / 25 bull, moved off the 15/50/35 house default by taking 10pp from the bull and giving it to the bear. Bear raised to 25% because three independent adverse paths are live and none is remote: (1) US MFN pricing and pharma tariffs, which management explicitly excludes from guidance so the guided numbers carry no allowance for them at all; (2) Cimzia, ~EUR 1.9bn/yr, has been biosimilar-free for over two years past LOE on manufacturing difficulty alone -- that is a reprieve, not a moat, and it can end in any quarter; (3) Briviact lost US exclusivity Feb-2026 with EU to follow Aug-2026 while Vimpat fell 41% in H1. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right together -- Bimzelx reaching EUR 7bn+ peak AND holding price as access widens (management itself flags net pricing erosion) AND the gMG duo scaling against argenx's Vyvgart AND the Candid/Neurona pipeline paying off. Base at 50%.

sanity_check.method: Step 8c. Ten years of Dec fiscal-year-end closes fetched from Yahoo (UCB.BR, 10y monthly), aligned to UCB's Dec-31 FY end, combined with each year's own net debt and share count to give a historical EV and multiple series. TTM built as FY2025 + H1-2026 - H1-2025.
sanity_check.commentary: PASS, with one flag. On TTM earnings UCB trades at 13.4x EV/EBITDA and 19.1x P/E against 10-year medians of 12.3x and 22.6x -- i.e. near or below its own historical middle, because earnings have genuinely grown into the multiple rather than the multiple having merely expanded. The model's weighted IV of EUR 201.33 implies 12.5x EV/EBITDA and 17.8x P/E, both comfortably inside the 10.0-25.2x and 15.7-48.4x historical bands and close to the medians, so the DCF is not asking the market to grant a multiple it has never granted -- the usual failure mode of a terminal-heavy build. THE FLAG: EV/Sales at 5.26x TTM (and 5.79x on FY2025) sits far above the 3.14x median and at the top of a 3.0-6.3x range whose upper end exists only in FY2024-25, the two Bimzelx re-rating years. The EBITDA and P/E multiples look benign only because margin has expanded from ~24% to ~40%; if that margin proves to be the cycle peak rather than the new normal, the sales multiple is the honest one and the stock is expensive. This is precisely the bear scenario, where the FY2035 EBITDA margin settles at 27% and IV falls to EUR 74.37.

historical_averages_ex_outliers.note: medians and full ranges over FY2016-FY2025 Dec closes; no years excluded

sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Implied 12.5x EV/EBITDA and 17.8x P/E at the weighted IV sit near the 10yr medians (12.3x / 22.6x). Flag retained: TTM EV/Sales 5.26x vs 3.14x median, top of a range whose upper end exists only in the FY2024-25 Bimzelx re-rating years -- earnings multiples look benign only because EBITDA margin expanded ~24% -> ~40%. If that margin is a cycle peak, EV/Sales is the honest multiple; that risk is carried in the bear case (27% terminal margin, IV EUR 74.37).
sanity_check.fix_applied: None required -- sanity check passed. FY2025 FCF was deliberately not mid-cycled (see valuation_philosophy); margin-peak risk is carried in the flows via a faded terminal margin rather than a mechanical haircut.

valuation_philosophy.model: Owner-FCF DCF, 10-year explicit component build, three scenarios, probability-weighted
valuation_philosophy.why_this_model: UCB is a conventional operating company -- patented branded pharmaceuticals sold for cash, with a real cash flow statement, real capex and real net debt. Routed to the owner-FCF DCF by row 1/2 of the dcf-methods table. None of the non-FCF families apply: it is not a bank, REIT, insurer, trust or distressed shell.
valuation_philosophy.why_10_years_not_5: The year-5 base-case owner-FCF margin is 22.8% and still climbing toward ~23%, and the whole thesis is a multi-year product-cycle ramp with patent runway disclosed to 2033/2035/2037. Capitalizing a still-ramping year-5 margin in perpetuity would systematically undervalue the business. Ten years carries the margin to maturity before the terminal value is struck.
valuation_philosophy.the_fy2025_base_question: THIS IS THE CENTRAL METHODOLOGICAL CHOICE AND IT IS DELIBERATE. FY2025 owner FCF of EUR 1,608m sits against an FY2015-2024 owner-FCF median of EUR 605m -- a 2.7x step. The house reflex for such a gap is to mid-cycle the peak back toward the median. THAT REFLEX IS REJECTED HERE, and the model is built off a normalized FORWARD base instead. The reason is that the FY2015-2024 median describes a company that no longer exists: it is the pre-Bimzelx UCB, a mature epilepsy franchise in slow decline. The step-change is a genuine product-cycle inflection, not a windfall -- Bimzelx alone did EUR 2,227m of net sales in FY2025 from a standing start and is guided to at least EUR 7bn at peak, with Rystiggo, Zilbrysq, Fintepla and the Evenity profit-share behind it. The five growth drivers went from 39% of net sales in H1-2025 to 54% in H1-2026. Critically, H1-2026 CONFIRMS the trajectory rather than reversing it: revenue EUR 4,270m (+22%), net income EUR 1,111m, adjusted EBITDA EUR 1,736m at a 40.7% margin against 29.6% a year earlier. Mid-cycling to EUR 605m would have valued a franchise that is demonstrably gone and produced a number with no informational content. What IS mid-cycled is the terminal margin: the base case lets the EBITDA margin peak at 37.5% and then FADE to 36.0%, and the bear case takes it to 27%, so the risk that 40.7% is the cycle peak is carried in the flows rather than in a mechanical haircut to the base.
valuation_philosophy.the_h1_2026_negative_fcf_question: H1-2026 free cash flow of EUR -77m is NOT treated as the run-rate, and the reason is visible line by line in the interim cash flow statement. Operating cash flow was a positive EUR 369m. The swing came from (i) a EUR -623m working-capital outflow driven by the growth itself -- receivables and inventory building behind a 22% revenue increase -- plus EUR -61m of working capital taken on with the acquisitions, and (ii) a capex step-up to EUR 446m in the half (PP&E 238 + intangibles 208) versus EUR 449m for the WHOLE of FY2025, reflecting the Georgia biologics campus build. Separately and below the FCF line, EUR -2,227m went out for Candid and Neurona; that is investing/M&A, not operating deterioration, and it does not touch the FCF definition used here at all. The underlying business in the same half earned EUR 1,111m of net income on a 40.7% adjusted EBITDA margin. The model does carry the lesson forward, though, in two places: capex starts at 8.0% of revenue in FY2026 (versus 5.8% in FY2025) before tapering to 5.5%, and the working-capital capture rate is set NEGATIVE at -12%, so growth consumes cash for the whole projection rather than releasing it.
valuation_philosophy.sbc_and_dilution: SBC of EUR 188m (2.43% of revenue) is fully expensed in the flows and the share count is held flat at the 193.95m fully diluted figure -- charged once, never both. UCB is a modest issuer by the standards of this folder, so the house/street band is narrow: EUR 201.33 house against EUR 221.66 street, a spread of only ~10% of the price. The band has NOT collapsed (this is not an SBC-zero market), so band_position is reported as a real number, 74.6% -- the market price sits close to the street ceiling, i.e. today's EUR 216.50 is roughly what you pay if you accept the sell-side convention of treating share-based comp as non-cash.
valuation_philosophy.conclusion: The honest answer is that UCB is FULLY VALUED to modestly overvalued at EUR 216.50. The probability-weighted intrinsic value is EUR 201.33, about 7% BELOW the market price, and the base case alone at EUR 206.80 is still below it. The bull case at EUR 317.34 shows there is real upside if Bimzelx reaches its guided peak with margins intact -- but the market is already paying for a meaningful share of that: the price implies a required return of only ~7.5%, and a 15% hurdle would need an entry around EUR 117. This is not a call that the business is bad. It is a very good business at a price that has already re-rated to reflect it, which is exactly what the Analysis JSON's own high-severity 'valuation / expectations risk' flags. The margin for error is thin: the bear case, which requires nothing more exotic than Cimzia biosimilars arriving, MFN pricing landing, and the 40.7% margin proving to be a peak, produces EUR 74.37.
